title: Merging arrays of DNF formulas preserves duplicate-free terms
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be two arrays of DNF formulas over $n$ variables, of lengths $m_1$ and $m_2$ respectively; write $g_1 \sqcup g_2$ for their merge, the array of length $m_1+m_2$ whose first $m_1$ entries are the formulas of $g_1$, in order, and whose remaining $m_2$ entries are those of $g_2$, in order. Suppose that every term occurring in any formula of $g_1$, and every term occurring in any formula of $g_2$, is a list of literals with no repetition. Then the same holds for the merged array: for every index $k$ and every term $t$ of the formula at position $k$ in $g_1 \sqcup g_2$, the literals of $t$ are pairwise distinct.
hypotheses_covered: every term of every formula in the first array has no repeated literal
every term of every formula in the second array has no repeated literal
k ranges over the indices of the merged array (of length m₁+m₂)
replaced:
If every term of every DNF gate of $g_1$ and of $g_2$ has no duplicate literals
($\mathrm{Nodup}$), then every term of every gate of the merged array
$\mathrm{mergeGates}\,g_1\,g_2$ likewise has no duplicate literals.
